title: Coordinates on a grid
keyIdea: (x, y) means go x across along the x-axis, then y up, starting from the origin (0, 0).

kid: A grid has two number lines. The x-axis goes across. The y-axis goes up. They meet at the origin, which is (0, 0).
A point is written (x, y). Go across first, then up. Think: along the corridor, then up the stairs. (3, 5) means 3 across and 5 up.
adult: The ordered pair (x, y) gives the distance across, then the distance up, from the origin. Order matters: (2, 5) and (5, 2) are different points.
Points on the x-axis have y = 0; points on the y-axis have x = 0. Distances along a grid line are easy: from (1, 4) to (6, 4) is 6 − 1 = 5 units.

familyTip: Play battleships on squared paper. Call out coordinates as (across, up).

practice.prompt: Which point is 4 across and 2 up?
How far is it from ({a}, 3) to ({b}, 3)?
practice.hint: Same height, so subtract the x-coordinates.

practice.prompt: A point is {a} across and {b} up. What is its x-coordinate?

choices: The origin, where the axes meet

pool.explain: It is 5 across and 0 up, so it is on the x-axis.

pool.prompt: In (3, 7), which number tells you how far up?

pool.explain: (2, 6) is 2 across; (6, 2) is 6 across. They are different.

pool.hint: Along the corridor, then up the stairs.
